candidates.name: strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (422 commits, GPL functions, dev-only via devtools::install_github) with the full UPGo STR analysis toolkit: cleaning/processing raw AirDNA property and daily files, compress/expand STR tables, 'raffle' probabilistic geocoding of listings to administrative geography, commercial-operator classification, frequently-rented entire-home detection, 'ghost hostel' cluster detection (private rooms in one unit run as a de facto hotel), and matching STR listings to actual housing units. No data files committed (methods/functions only) — it is the reference implementation the McGill Urban Politics and Governance (UPGo) lab uses to process licensed AirDNA extracts.
candidates.why_useful: This is the canonical open-source method for turning raw STR panel data (AirDNA-style property/daily records) into occupancy, ADR, commercial-operator share, and housing-unit-linkage metrics — directly useful as a methodology reference for gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) and #8/#9 (STR supply classification) if we ever obtain any AirDNA-like sample, and its raffle/ghost-hotel logic is reusable on our own Inside Airbnb panel.
candidates.geography: generic (Canada/US-focused lab but code is geography-agnostic)
candidates.license: unspecified on repo (GPL-3.0 on sibling raffle/ghost packages)

candidates.name: upgo
candidates.what_it_holds: The lab's general-purpose R utility package (DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE, R/ and man/ folders). Companion package to strr; likely holds shared helpers (DB connections, plotting themes, geocoding helpers) used across all UPGo city reports. No committed datasets found in the repo tree.
candidates.why_useful: Minor — mostly plumbing for the lab's other repos, but worth knowing it exists if any of the report repos import it as a dependency and we want to reproduce their pipeline.

candidates.name: raffle
candidates.what_it_holds: Standalone R package implementing the 'raffle' method: probabilistically assigns STR listings (given only an approximate/obfuscated map point, as Airbnb/AirDNA show) to administrative geography (city, neighbourhood, census tract) by weighted random assignment matching known listing-density priors.
candidates.why_useful: Reusable geocoding method for our own Inside Airbnb 123-market panel, where Airbnb's public listing lat/long is deliberately jittered — could sharpen neighbourhood-level assignment for regional/city splits.

candidates.name: ghost
candidates.what_it_holds: Standalone R package (spun out of strr) implementing the 'ghost hotel/hostel' detector: identifies clusters of private-room STR listings that are actually being run as a single commercial operation out of one building/unit.
candidates.why_useful: Could be applied to our Inside Airbnb panel to estimate the commercial/multi-listing share of supply, a proxy for professionalised vs. casual host mix that feeds nights/ADR interpretation.

candidates.name: vancouver-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Full bookdown report repo (00-executive_summary.Rmd ... 05-references.Rmd) plus a committed data/ folder: data/cmhc/ has CMHC annual rental-market-survey workbooks (annual_avg_rent_2015-2019.xlsx, annual_units_2015-2019.xlsx ~1.1MB each, annual_vacancy_2015-2019.xlsx ~1.5MB each, plus condensed van_avg_rent.csv, van_units.csv, van_vacancy.csv) by Vancouver neighbourhood; data/shapefiles/ has CMHC_NBHD_2016 neighbourhood boundary shapefile (16MB .shp), a Vancouver business-licences shapefile (85MB .dbf — city business licence registry, likely including STR operator licences), a local-area-boundary shapefile, and a rapid-transit-station point shapefile; plus a van_scrape.Rdata (Airbnb/STR scrape snapshot). Covers 'regulatory impacts' and 'COVID returning listings' analysis, 2015-2020ish.
candidates.why_useful: Committed CMHC rental vacancy/rent/unit-count tables by Vancouver neighbourhood (2015-2019) are exactly the free, public LTR housing-economics panel named in gap #13 (STR<->LTR crossover), and the business-licence shapefile is a real municipal STR-adjacent registry (gap #12) with geographic boundaries attached.
candidates.time_coverage: 2015-2020 (CMHC tables); business licence shapefile vintage unclear
candidates.size_hint: ~227 MB repo (dominated by the 85MB business-licences.dbf and 16MB neighbourhood shapefile)

candidates.name: vancouver-regulations
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of STR host compliance with Vancouver's 2018 STR licensing regulations. Committed data/raffle.csv (~7.7 MB) — appears to be the output of the raffle geocoding method applied to Vancouver STR listings, i.e. a listing-level (or listing-day-level) dataset with assigned neighbourhood/geography and likely licence-compliance flags.
candidates.why_useful: A concrete point-in-time compliance dataset for a real STR ordinance (Vancouver 2018) — useful as a case study or calibration set for regulatory-impact modelling (gap #12), and shows what a raffle-processed listing file looks like in practice.

candidates.name: cmhcr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package described as 'Import and Clean CMHC Data Tables' — a client/parser for Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation rental market survey data tables (the same CMHC series seen packaged as raw xlsx in vancouver-analysis). No committed data itself; it is the pull/clean tool.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made client for a public, national (Canada-wide) rental-market data source — could pull CMHC vacancy/rent series for any Canadian metro, feeding STR<->LTR crossover and housing-supply-economics angles (gap #13) without re-scraping CMHC by hand.

candidates.name: canada-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Replication/analysis code repo explicitly tied to 'Analysis of Airbnb activity in Canada, for Combs et al. 2019' — an academic paper on Airbnb activity across Canadian cities. Small repo (117 KB), R/ folder and README only; no large data files visible in top-level listing (README not fully retrievable).
candidates.why_useful: An academic replication package tied to a named, citable paper on Airbnb activity in Canada — worth flagging as a possible source of methodology or (if the underlying data is linked in the README) a multi-city Canadian Airbnb panel predating our own Inside Airbnb coverage.
candidates.size_hint: 117 KB (code only, per repo API size field)

candidates.name: bc-report-2024
candidates.what_it_holds: R/ and output/ folders for the lab's 2024 British Columbia STR report (province-wide, following BC's short-term rental legislation). No data/ folder visible in the top-level tree (likely pulls from a private DB), so this is analysis code, not a committed dataset. Sibling repos bc-report-2022 and bc-report-2023-summer are the same report series in earlier years.
candidates.why_useful: Shows the lab publishes an annual province-wide BC STR report; the code/methodology could be reused even without the underlying (likely proprietary AirDNA-sourced) data, and any published PDF/output linked from it may contain BC-wide STR volume estimates useful as an external benchmark.

candidates.name: toronto-report-2023
candidates.what_it_holds: Toronto STR/MTR (mid-term rental) market report code, ~8.4 MB repo, R/ and output/ folders. Sibling to toronto-report (2021) and toronto-analysis (2019), forming a multi-year Toronto STR report series from the same lab.
candidates.why_useful: Multi-year Toronto STR report series is a longer time-series of a single city's regulatory/market narrative than we currently hold for any Canadian market; worth reading the output/ PDFs if the underlying data isn't public.

candidates.name: montreal-finance-2022
candidates.what_it_holds: Code for the paper 'High rises and housing stress: A spatial big-data analysis of rental housing financialization' — includes R/, latex/, stan/ (Bayesian spatial model) and output/ folders. An academic paper replication package on rental-housing financialization and displacement in Montreal.
candidates.why_useful: A named academic paper's full replication package (including Stan model code) on rental-market financial stress — tangential to Airbnb directly but relevant to the STR<->LTR housing-supply-economics angle (gap #13) in a major Canadian market Airbnb operates in.
candidates.size_hint: unspecified, contains stan/ and latex/ subfolders

candidates.name: mtl_landlords
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (scraper/, captcha_solver/, notebooks/, session_handling/) to pull Montreal landlord/property data, apparently from the municipal property-tax roll ('matricule' numbers — download_matricule_nrs.py, scrape_batch.py). Includes htmls/ and data/ folders (contents not enumerated here).
candidates.why_useful: A working scraper (non-Airbnb site — Montreal municipal property registry) for landlord/ownership records, which could support housing-supply/STR-conversion analysis if ever run; flagged as method only per the no-scraping rule.

candidates.name: STRresearch
candidates.what_it_holds: Small independent (non-UPGo) repo described only as 'STR Research for AirDNA'. Contents not retrievable via WebFetch (README not rendered); found via GitHub code search on 'airdna'. Unverified — flagged for a future scout to open directly with an authenticated GitHub view.
candidates.why_useful: Possible small AirDNA-adjacent dataset or analysis; low confidence given inability to verify contents in this pass.

candidates.name: airdna (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Not a data repo — an independent third-party API-surface profile/documentation of the commercial AirDNA Enterprise API (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates), maintained by 'API Evangelist' as part of a series cataloguing many APIs. Documents endpoints and data structure, not actual pulled data.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only as a map of what AirDNA's paid API exposes (market-level occupancy/ADR/revenue metrics across 120,000+ markets) in case the team ever evaluates a paid AirDNA subscription or needs to know what fields such a feed would contain.

notes: WebSearch's shared session budget was exhausted (200/200) before any query for this theme returned results, and the DuckDuckGo HTML fallback served a CAPTCHA page instead of results, so this scout ran entirely on `gh search repos`/`gh api` plus WebFetch against GitHub itself. That combination worked well here because the theme's exact keyword ('strr', 'UPGo-McGill') is a precise GitHub org/repo name, so `gh search repos "strr"` surfaced UPGo-McGill/strr directly, and from there `gh api users/UPGo-McGill/repos --paginate` gave a complete 58-repo org inventory to triage by content listing. The single best find is UPGo-McGill/vancouver-analysis, which has a genuinely large committed data/ folder (CMHC rental-market tables 2015-2019 by Vancouver neighbourhood, plus a business-licence shapefile) — this is public CMHC data, not licensed, and fills the housing/STR-crossover gap (#13) with real files rather than a pointer. Most other UPGo report repos (bc-report-*, toronto-report-*, la-report-2021, ottawa-2021, citq-rapport-2024, ontario-report-2024) contain only R/ and output/ code with no committed source data — they likely pull from a private lab database or licensed AirDNA extract not present in the public repo, so their value is methodological/narrative (annual STR report PDFs in output/) rather than raw data. Two smaller GPL packages (raffle, ghost) spun out of strr are worth remembering as reusable geocoding/cluster-detection methods applicable to our own Inside Airbnb panel. Did not verify mtl_landlords/data or STRresearch contents in depth — worth a follow-up GitHub-code-search pass by another scout with a fresh WebSearch budget, and worth checking if any UPGo report repo's output/ PDF is browsable for headline BC/Toronto/Ontario STR volume numbers as an external cross-check series.
